indicators.title: Housing Affordability Index (NAR)
indicators.context: The National Association of Realtors index: 100 means the median-income family can just barely afford the median home. Higher is better — the historical norm is 130-180.
indicators.read: The affordability index is 106 — the median family barely qualifies for the median home.

indicators.title: Mortgage Debt Service · % of income
indicators.context: Mortgage payments as a share of household disposable income (quarterly) — how heavy the aggregate mortgage burden actually is.
indicators.read: The mortgage-payment share of disposable income is 5.9%, up 0.2 points from a year ago.

indicators.title: Mortgage Delinquency Rate · banks
indicators.context: The share of single-family mortgages at commercial banks that are past due (quarterly) — where affordability stress turns into credit stress.
indicators.read: Just 1.9% of mortgages are delinquent — homeowners are keeping up.

indicators.title: 30-Year Fixed Mortgage Rate
indicators.context: The average rate on a 30-year fixed home loan — the input behind the affordability squeeze above: it sets what a buyer can afford each month.
indicators.read: 30-year mortgages are at 6.48% — above the comfort zone for most budgets.
